subject.title: browser tool: include current page URL in before_tool_call params for act/type actions

question: Should OpenClaw expose a policy-checked current browser tab URL to `before_tool_call` handlers for browser `act`/`type`, and should that surface be hook-param enrichment or a query/context helper?
rationale: This changes the plugin API and security boundary for browser URLs; automation can implement a chosen contract, but should not pick URL leakage, redaction, and compatibility semantics by itself.

options.title: Add hook-time URL contract
options.body: Expose an additive, policy-checked current URL for browser `act`/`type` before plugin hooks decide whether to rewrite, block, or approve the tool call.

options.title: Expose a query helper
options.body: Keep hook params unchanged and add a supported hook context/query helper for plugins that need the active browser URL at decision time.

options.title: Keep plugin workaround only
options.body: Leave URL caching and fail-secure behavior to credential plugins, accepting the cold-cache limitation and duplicated plugin complexity.

recommendation.title: Add hook-time URL contract
recommendation.body: Expose an additive, policy-checked current URL for browser `act`/`type` before plugin hooks decide whether to rewrite, block, or approve the tool call.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history signal is browser tool/runtime and safe URL response work adjacent to this contract.
